negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage of occupied-territory successor institutions is absent from this slice.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Half the 'legacy entity' question — what happened to the branch estate and payment infrastructure after Ukrainian banks exited — is invisible without it, and those entities are also sanctions-relevant, which constrains any collection.

negative_findings.description: I had no established Ukrainian vocabulary for web archiving of corporate disclosure specifically: terms like 'веб-архів', 'знімок сторінки', 'архівна копія сайту' returned generic or unrelated results, and Ukrainian-language searches did not surface any archiving service or project aimed at financial-sector websites.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language terminology for this cell's core concept is thin, so uk-language search recall for archiving infrastructure is inherently poor; uk searches were productive only for the REGISTER side (НБУ/ФГВФО/SMIDA), not the ARCHIVE side.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future runs should search the register/liquidation vocabulary in Ukrainian and the archiving vocabulary in English, rather than expecting both in one language.

negative_findings.description: archive.today/archive.ph is documented as serving bot challenges to automated clients and has no official API. I did not attempt a fetch, so its accessibility here is a hypothesis, not a verdict.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treat archive.ph as manual-only until a deterministic pass tests it.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If archive.ph is unusable at scale, IA becomes the sole automatable archive and its robots-based exclusions become an unmitigated blind spot.

negative_findings.description: No archived-disclosure source was found for Ukrainian PSPs / non-bank payment institutions (e.g. Portmone, EasyPay, City24, IBox, Fondy). Searching for archived Ukrainian PSP investor/disclosure pages surfaced only bank material; PSPs are mostly private LLCs with no statutory issuer disclosure, so SMIDA does not cover them.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSP-side archival continuity is unaddressed in this slice despite sector=both.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payments-side history (fee schedules, network partners, ownership announcements) exists only on the PSPs' own sites, making it uniquely vulnerable and uniquely dependent on proactive Wayback save-page-now capture.

negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf or NCR/NCR Atleos press release announcing an ATM or branch-automation contract with a named Ukrainian bank (Oschadbank, PrivatBank or others) surfaced in English-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned only global Diebold Nixdorf/NCR strategy coverage, an unrelated FOREX go-live release, and SEC filings — nothing Ukraine-specific. This is a search negative, not evidence that no such deal or release exists; the OEM newsrooms and atmmarketplace hubs were not exhaustively paged.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Global ATM OEM engagement in Ukraine is a core question for this cell. If the OEMs genuinely do not publish Ukrainian wins, the estate must be reconstructed from Prozorro award records and local service companies instead of vendor PR.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language search terms were established for the global ATM OEMs' local entities. Queries mixing 'Diebold Nixdorf'/'NCR' with Ukrainian words were not run in this pass, and the transliterations ('Дібольд Ніксдорф', 'ЕН-СІ-АР', 'Ей-Ті-Ем груп') are untested guesses.
negative_findings.result_summary: The one attempted transliteration probe ('Ей Ті Ем') returned nothing relevant — only bank ATM-location maps, i.e. the term is heavily noisy in Ukrainian.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language coverage is mandatory and the ATM-hardware sub-segment currently rests on English sources plus one local service company (Printec Ukraine). Ukrainian legal-entity names are needed to query the state register and local press.

negative_findings.description: The Ukrainian terms 'банкомат' and 'POS-термінал' are dominated by consumer-facing content — bank branch/ATM location maps, merchant acquiring sales pages and PRRO retail shops — rather than supplier or procurement information.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both the POS-supplier and Printec queries returned mostly privatbank.ua/map, pumb.ua/map, universalbank.com.ua/map and terminal e-shops.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated collection on these terms needs vendor-name or procurement-vocabulary anchors ('постачальник', 'закупівля', 'ДК 021', 'впровадження', 'сервісне обслуговування') or it will drown in retail noise.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found of BPC Banking Technologies (SmartVista), OpenWay (Way4) or Temenos engagements with Ukrainian banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: The combined English query surfaced only Tietoevry/UPC material; no BPC, OpenWay or Temenos Ukraine announcement appeared. Not searched in Ukrainian ('Смарт Віста', 'Вей4', 'Теменос') in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These three are the most likely international card-processing/core-banking suppliers in the CIS/CEE region; their absence or presence in Ukraine materially shapes the competitive map. Currently unresolved rather than negative.

negative_findings.description: No card-personalisation or card-issuance vendor announcement (IDEMIA, Thales/Gemalto, Giesecke+Devrient) naming a Ukrainian bank was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: The English query returned only global metal-card rankings, an Egypt biometric-card contest and a Madagascar ID contract — nothing Ukrainian. Ukrainian-language equivalents ('персоналізація карток', 'виробництво платіжних карток') were not queried in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card manufacturing/personalisation is a recurring capex line for issuers and is normally announced by the supplier, not the bank; a blind spot here leaves issuance-side infrastructure unmapped.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian in-country distributor of Ingenico, PAX or Verifone POS hardware was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: The query returned only North American and Western European distributors (POSDATA, DCCSupply, paymentdiscounter). The Ukrainian-language part of the query did not pull local distributor pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The terminal distribution channel determines who actually supplies acquiring banks in Ukraine. Without it, the POS hardware supply chain must be inferred from bank acquiring pages, reseller catalogues and Prozorro awards.

negative_findings.description: None of the listed candidate URLs were fetched or liveness-checked in this pass — all were recorded from search-result metadata and snippets.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs are provided with confidence scores only; no claim is made that any is reachable. Access-status fields (e.g. suspected paywalls at youcontrol.com.ua and finclub.net, suspected registration wall at playtender.com.ua) are hypotheses.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A downstream deterministic verification pass must confirm liveness and access; a 403 or timeout on any of these should be treated as bot defence, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: No TED notice specifically for banking or payment services in Ukraine was surfaced by search; the only concrete Ukraine-related TED notice found was for security services to the EU Delegation to Ukraine (notice 151645-2025).
negative_findings.result_summary: TED is confirmed as a relevant channel, but no banking/payments Ukraine notice was actually located in this pass. Requires a CPV-filtered search on the TED site itself.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents overstating EU-funded banking procurement volume for Ukraine; the channel is a hypothesis until a CPV 66xxxxxx + Ukraine query returns hits.

negative_findings.description: Searches on Mintsyfra/Diia payment procurement returned platform-administration and Diia.ID tenders, but no lot explicitly for 'платіжний шлюз' / 'еквайринг' inside state e-services.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Diia payment-rail procurement, if it exists, may be embedded inside broader IT administration contracts or handled by a bank under a non-procurement arrangement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The commercial terms of payment acceptance in Diia are strategically important and appear not to be exposed as a standalone tender — a structural blind spot rather than a search failure.

negative_findings.description: URLs for dasu.gov.ua and the center.diia.gov.ua library article were not fetched in this pass; the Diia slug in particular was transcribed from a search result.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence rather than asserted as reachable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids a false liveness claim ahead of the deterministic verification pass.

negative_findings.description: AMCU has published notices about changes to the publication of appeals-body decisions, implying the decision corpus may not be consistently or fully published on amcu.gov.ua over time.
negative_findings.result_summary: Appeal decisions are best collected via the tender record in ProZorro or via aggregators (Clarity) rather than assuming a complete AMCU archive.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collection routine pointed only at amcu.gov.ua would silently under-collect disputes on banking lots.

negative_findings.description: A direct fetch of the RBI investor reports hub (https://www.rbinternational.com/en/investors/reports.html) returned report categories (semi-annual, annual, quarterly, regulatory disclosures) and headline metrics, but no mention of Ukraine on the landing page itself — only repeated 'excl. Russia' framing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukraine-specific figures are not exposed on the IR landing page; they live inside the report PDFs and the XLSM results file, so the landing page alone is not a usable extraction target.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must go one level deeper (into the PDF/XLSM artefacts) rather than scraping the IR index; a shallow crawler would wrongly conclude RBI does not report Ukraine.

negative_findings.description: No named 'Ukraine segment' was found in Crédit Agricole S.A. group-level reporting; searches surfaced only the Ukrainian subsidiary's own site as the source of Ukraine P&L and ratios.
negative_findings.result_summary: Crédit Agricole's Ukraine disclosure is subsidiary-published (credit-agricole.ua press centre + documents page), not parent-segment-published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's premise (Ukraine data hiding inside Vienna/Budapest/Paris group reports) holds strongly for RBI, OTP and ProCredit but only weakly for Paris; collection design must differ per parent.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief names a 'Pyrkal/Bank Pivdenny-type minority' foreign-stake tier. Searching in Ukrainian for Bank Pivdenny management reports and foreign shareholders did not return a foreign parent group publishing a Ukraine segment or country annex.
negative_findings.result_summary: No foreign-parent IR channel identified for Bank Pivdenny; only local/media profiles were found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For minority-foreign-stake banks the group-disclosure channel appears absent, so this tier must be covered by local statutory disclosure (NBU, SMIDA, bank site) instead — a different collection design.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language equivalent of parent-group 'segment reporting' vocabulary was found in use on parent IR sites; Ukrainian search terms only reach subsidiary-level documents (річний звіт, фінансова звітність, звіт про управління).
negative_findings.result_summary: Parent-group Ukraine annexes exist only in EN (and HU/DE for OTP/RBI/ProCredit domestic filings); uk-language search cannot reach them.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A uk-only crawl systematically misses the group channel, and an en-only crawl misses the local statutory channel — both language passes are structurally required for this cell.

negative_findings.description: The intuitive domain bankvostok.com.ua did not surface as Bank Vostok's live disclosure site; all real documents resolve to vstbank.ua (and a legacy content host content.vostok.bank), consistent with a rebrand to «ВСТ БАНК».
negative_findings.result_summary: Searching the assumed domain returned unrelated banks (PrivatBank, Industrialbank) plus vstbank.ua PDFs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector keyed to bankvostok.com.ua would record a false dead source; the correct base domain must be vstbank.ua.

negative_findings.description: No successor institution to АКБ «Конкорд» was found. NBU revoked its licence on 01.08.2023 for AML violations and the Deposit Guarantee Fund completed liquidation on 05.05.2026. No evidence links Concord's business to Fintech Band/monobank or any other bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only liquidation coverage (NBU, DGF, media); no acquiring bank, no transferred portfolio, no archived disclosure page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief names 'Concord successors' as a target; for source-scouting purposes that target does not exist as a live disclosure publisher and should be re-scoped to DGF liquidation records and web archives.

negative_findings.description: universalbank.com.ua (monobank's licensed bank) returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch of its financial-reports page.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on https://www.universalbank.com.ua/financial-reports; the page is indexed in search and other pages on the domain are referenced normally.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most important source in the cell. It must be treated as bot-defended-but-live and collected via a browser-based fetcher, not marked dead.

negative_findings.description: a-bank.com.ua/about/reports returned only a shell page titled «Регулярна інформація» with no document links in the HTML.
negative_findings.result_summary: Content is loaded client-side; document files are served through /backend/api/v1/pages/media/file?path=...
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A static-HTML crawler will silently collect zero A-Bank documents; headless rendering or direct use of the media API is required.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated investor-relations portal exists for Ukrainian domestic private banks. Each bank publishes under its own «розкриття інформації» / «фінансова звітність» heading with a different URL scheme, file-naming convention and CMS.
negative_findings.result_summary: Five banks examined used five different document path patterns (Drupal /sites/default/files, SparkFile CMS, backend media API, /docs/accounting/annual/{year}, /storage/files).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be per-bank bespoke; only SMIDA/stockmarket.gov.ua offer a uniform fallback, and only for issuer-format filings.

negative_findings.description: The English concept 'investor relations' has no consistent Ukrainian counterpart on these banks' sites; the functional equivalents are «інформація для акціонерів та стейкхолдерів», «регульована інформація емітента» and «загальні збори акціонерів».
negative_findings.result_summary: Querying with IR-style English terms returned mostly PUMB (the only bank with a true EN IR section); local queries were required for all others.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: English-only discovery would have found roughly one of the ~15 disclosure pages in this cell; local-language querying is not optional here.

negative_findings.description: I found no evidence of a sector/KVED or 'banks only' filter within the SMIDA issuer database or the stockmarket.gov.ua participant index. The fetched /db/emitent page did not document search parameters, filters or URL query structure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Issuer enumeration for banking/payments will have to be done by joining EDRPOU codes from external registers (NBU licensed banks, payment-institution registers, ЄДР) against the issuer index, not by a native sector filter.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Materially changes the collection design: the disclosure system is a confirmation and enrichment layer keyed by EDRPOU, not a self-serve sector screen.

negative_findings.description: The stockmarket.gov.ua open-data API index page states that data is available through 30 June 2021, matching the site's 'Опублікування регульованої інформації (до 30/06/2021)' archive label.
negative_findings.result_summary: The v1 API appears to be a historical archive; post-July-2021 regulated information appears to flow through the SMIDA /db/feed stream and authorised regulated-information publishers instead. I did not find a documented successor API.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A pipeline built only on the v1 API would silently stop at mid-2021 and miss all recent bank filings.

negative_findings.description: Ukrainian-language searching for the register of 'осіб, які провадять діяльність з оприлюднення регульованої інформації' returned the legal framework (Положення z1307-23) and general descriptions, but I did not locate a public list page enumerating the licensed publishers.
negative_findings.result_summary: The existence of the role is confirmed by regulation; the enumerated register was not found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If issuers may publish via multiple authorised publishers, monitoring only SMIDA may leave gaps for some bank issuers.

negative_findings.description: stockmarket.gov.ua lists a 'Prospectuses' category in its participant navigation, but I did not find a documented direct URL for a searchable prospectus register, and searches for a bank bond prospectus register returned only procedural/administrative-service pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Prospectus discovery is currently hypothesised to run through the stockmarket.gov.ua prospectus section, the State Register of Securities Issues and the /db/feed 'проспект' report type — none confirmed as a standalone register UI.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bond prospectuses are the richest single artefact for a bank's funding strategy and risk disclosures; an unresolved access path is a real gap.

negative_findings.description: stockmarket.gov.ua exposes /db/login and /registration/user; the login page states that general information about issuers, exchanges, traders and rating agencies is freely accessible while 'перегляд інформації' and the pre-30/06/2021 disclosure-subject area use authorisation forms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Most of the value appears public, but some views may require a free account. Not tested — I did not create an account.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design should assume an anonymous path first and flag any view that turns out to be account-gated rather than assuming the whole database is open.

negative_findings.description: Ukrainian-language searching linking the NSSMC disclosure system to payments companies (платіжні установи, фінансові компанії) surfaced no payments-specific disclosure pathway; results were dominated by banks and general corporate issuers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Non-bank payments firms in Ukraine are typically LLCs rather than joint-stock companies and so mostly fall outside issuer disclosure, unless they issue bonds.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This cell should be treated as strong for banks and weak for pure payments actors; payments coverage must come from NBU/other registers.

negative_findings.description: Repeated Ukrainian-language searches for annual reports or financial statements published by Portmone, Fondy, EasyPay, IBOX, City24, LeoGaming or Maxi returned no company-published annual report or IR page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search results surfaced only third-party comparison articles, marketing pages and the open-data reporting portal. No 'річний звіт' PDF or investor-relations section was found for any of these brands.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The default assumption that licensed PSPs run investor-facing disclosure does not hold in Ukraine: apart from NovaPay, this layer is disclosure-silent and must be reconstructed from statutory filings and the regulator's register.

negative_findings.description: No press room or corporate press-release section was located for the 'Максі' / Maxi paysystems brand named in the cell scope.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian brand-plus-licence query returned nothing attributable to a Maxi payment operator; the brand may be defunct, renamed, or trading under a differently named legal entity.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The actor name in the cell brief may be stale. Entity resolution must run off the NBU register rather than off brand names.

negative_findings.description: The NSSMC issuer-disclosure system (stockmarket.gov.ua / SMIDA) was probed as a route to regulated disclosure by bond-issuing payment groups, but no direct landing URL was confirmed in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: The disclosure-portal query returned association and academic results instead; the portal itself was not reached, so it is recorded as an unconfirmed hypothesis rather than a candidate.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For NovaPay Credit and any other PSP that issues public bonds, the securities-regulator disclosure system is the mandatory-filing channel and would be a high-value source; it needs a follow-up pass.

negative_findings.description: The direct downloadable file of the Register of Payment Infrastructure was not isolated to a single confirmed URL in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search confirmed the register exists and is maintained under bank.gov.ua supervision pages, but the specific export endpoint was not pinned down; recorded at the section level with medium confidence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The register export is the backbone of the actor map for this cell; the exact endpoint should be resolved by a browsing pass before collection is automated.

negative_findings.description: Neither Visa nor Mastercard publishes Ukraine-specific volume, card-count or interchange disclosure. Ukraine-level scheme figures found in the press are consistently attributed to the NBU, not to the schemes.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in uk and en for Visa/Mastercard Ukraine results releases; only NBU-sourced share figures and generic marketing press surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-level UA numbers must be sourced from the regulator, not from scheme IR; do not expect an earnings-style series from the international schemes.

negative_findings.description: No published annual report or audited operational report for UPC, UkrCard, TAS Link or the EasyPay processing entity was located on the open web; volume claims ('400M+ transactions/year') come from company marketing pages and third-party profiles.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in en and uk for processor annual reports/processing volumes; only marketing copy, LinkedIn/Crunchbase profiles and NBU designation notices found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Processing-volume estimates must be treated as vendor claims; audited numbers, if any, will only appear via SMIDA issuer filings for the PrJSC-form entities.

negative_findings.description: bank.gov.ua returned HTTP 403 on a direct statistics-page fetch, while its PDF assets and news pages are indexed and reachable in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: WebFetch of https://bank.gov.ua/ua/statistic/sector-payment -> 403 Forbidden.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source for this cell is bot-defended; collection must use a browser-grade client. This is a hypothesis of bot protection, not evidence the site is down.

negative_findings.description: The NBU-designated important operator 'ТОВ ЕЙСІ ДІСКІ ПРОЦЕСІНГ' was not conclusively mapped to a public consumer brand/domain during this pass; the EasyPay association is an inference.
negative_findings.result_summary: Registry-derived legal name found, but no confirmed corporate site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents mis-attribution of processing volumes to the wrong brand.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Ukrainian for a DGF dataset presence on Ukraine's national open-data portal (data.gov.ua) covering banks in liquidation, payouts or asset sales. No DGF dataset page was surfaced by search; all results pointed back to fg.gov.ua HTML pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not confirm any machine-readable DGF dataset on data.gov.ua. Not a verdict that none exists — search recall was the limit, and the portal was not queried directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no structured open-data feed exists, all DGF collection must be HTML scraping of article-style pages plus PDF parsing, which is fragile and raises the cost of the collection layer. Worth a direct check of data.gov.ua's own search before committing to a scraper-only design.

negative_findings.description: Two Prozorro.Sale pages (the bankrupt-bank asset-sales landing page and the open-data page) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on plain fetch, while the same URLs appear as normal indexed results in search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as bot-defended-but-presumed-live rather than dead. The specific open-data/API endpoint list for the ЦБД1 bankrupt-bank asset stream could therefore not be enumerated in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prozorro.Sale holds the lot-level auction outcomes that the DGF site only aggregates. Without confirming the API surface, the collection plan for asset-sale pricing remains unspecified. A browser-based or properly-headered fetch should be retried before any liveness verdict.

negative_findings.description: The DGF annual-report landing pages were identified (article URLs per year), but the direct file URLs of the attached PDF/XLS annual report and audited financial statements were not individually enumerated in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Year-level article URLs captured for 2021-2025; per-file attachment URLs unresolved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collection pipeline needs the attachment URL pattern (likely under /storage/files/) to fetch the actual financial statements rather than the wrapper page. A single fetch of one report article will resolve this.

negative_findings.description: IADI's respondent-level annual survey data — which would contain Ukraine's own answers on resolution powers, funding and coverage — is members-only; only summary findings are public.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public summaries usable; granular Ukraine record requires a membership or a research-access request.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Peer benchmarking of the Ukrainian failed-bank regime will be coarse unless access is requested. This is an access-negotiation item, not a discovery failure.

negative_findings.description: No established Ukrainian-language term was found for a consolidated, cross-bank 'failed bank financial condition' dataset analogous to the US FDIC's failed-bank list with financials. The DGF's own vocabulary decomposes into per-process terms ('ліквідаційна маса', 'надходження', 'задоволення вимог кредиторів') rather than one dataset name.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched with several constructed Ukrainian phrasings; only the per-process pages surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design for this cell must target the process vocabulary, not a dataset name. Analysts expecting an FDIC-style single table will need to assemble it from the per-bank subdomains and the receipts/statistics articles.

negative_findings.description: The NBU no longer maintains its own Register of audit firms entitled to audit banks. Search evidence indicates that after Law 2258-VIII took effect on 2018-10-01 this function moved to the auditor register (now held by APOB). The historic NBU list (e.g. постанова v0640500-08 on diagnostic-survey audit firms) survives only as archival legislation.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live NBU-maintained bank-auditor register found; eligibility is determined by Section IV of the APOB register instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the collector from wasting cycles hunting a bank.gov.ua auditor list, and pins APOB as the single eligibility authority for A1 verification.

negative_findings.description: No central Ukrainian repository of auditor transparency reports (звіти про прозорість) was found. Each audit entity self-publishes its Art.37 report on its own website at its own URL pattern and cadence (PwC, KPMG, EY, Grant Thornton, SOVA-Audit all differ).
negative_findings.result_summary: Transparency reports are discoverable only firm-by-firm; APOB publishes registers and inspection results but was not observed to host a transparency-report index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be driven from the APOB Section IV firm list outward to per-firm websites, which is fragile and needs per-firm URL rules plus dead-link handling.

negative_findings.description: Deloitte Ukraine's Ukrainian-language звіт про прозорість was referenced in search summaries as existing for 2024, but no direct PDF/landing URL was surfaced in this pass; only impact report, management report and financial-statements pages were located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Deloitte transparency-report URL unresolved; recorded as unverified, not absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deloitte is a significant Ukrainian bank auditor; a missing transparency report leaves a hole in the auditor→bank mapping for its clients.

negative_findings.description: The APOB register search interface (register.apob.org.ua) was not machine-inspected in this pass, so it is unknown whether it exposes a JSON/API endpoint, supports filtering to Section IV only, or requires JS rendering.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register access mechanics unverified; the data.gov.ua dataset is the safer bulk fallback.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether auditor eligibility can be joined programmatically or must be re-derived from periodic open-data dumps.

negative_findings.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: APOB offers ?lang=en URLs but content is largely Ukrainian; transparency reports are predominantly Ukrainian-only (EY published Ukrainian versions; no consistent English series was found for the Ukrainian member firms).
negative_findings.result_summary: English-only collection would miss almost the entire cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms mandatory uk-language pipeline with Ukrainian-language OCR/NLP for PDF parsing.

negative_findings.description: No IFI project disclosure source was found that is specifically about Ukrainian PAYMENTS infrastructure (acquiring, card schemes, instant payments, POS) as opposed to bank lending. IFC advisory on credit reporting and EBRD TC with the NBU on financial-sector strategy are the closest, and both are credit/regulatory rather than payments-market disclosure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches across IFC, EBRD, EIB and WB surfaced overwhelmingly SME-lending, guarantee and risk-sharing facilities; payments appears only incidentally inside broader financial-sector programmes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For a payments-sector intelligence workstream, IFI disclosure will under-serve the payments half of the cell and must be complemented by NBU and scheme-level sources handled by other cells.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language mirror of IFI project-level disclosure databases was found. EBRD PSDs, IFC SIIs, MIGA project briefs and World Bank project documents for Ukraine bank transactions appear in English only; Ukrainian-language coverage comes from government republication (MoF, NBU MEFP translations), partner-bank pages and media, not from the IFIs' own registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian queries returned MoF/NBU/KMU pages, bank programme pages, Wikipedia and press (ZN.ua, Forbes.ua, Ekonomichna Pravda) rather than any uk-language IFI project register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring of this cell must target the Ukrainian intermediaries, not the IFIs; entity resolution needs a maintained ЄБРР/МФК/ЄІБ/БАГІ/МБРР alias table.

negative_findings.description: The EBRD project search interface applies filters client-side rather than through URL query parameters, so there is no stable deep-link for 'Ukraine + Financial Institutions + last 12 months'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Direct fetch of the EBRD projects portal showed a filter UI (country, sector, status, document type, date range) but 'dynamic filtering through the interface rather than URL parameters'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated EBRD collection needs a headless browser or an undocumented backing JSON endpoint; naive HTTP scraping will silently return unfiltered or empty results.

negative_findings.description: openaid.gov.ua was found as the Ukrainian aid-transparency register but its current data coverage and update cadence were not established, and it was reached over plain HTTP.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only an 'About' page surfaced; described in secondary sources as a promised portal covering all IFI/donor-supported projects.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It could be either the best Ukrainian-language crosswalk for IFI project names or an abandoned portal; must be verified before being relied on.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief anticipates 'financial covenants' in IFI disclosure. No public IFI document was found that reproduces bank-level financial covenants (capital, NPL, liquidity triggers) for a Ukrainian bank borrower.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSDs/SIIs disclose instrument type, size, use of proceeds, ownership and E&S category, but covenant schedules sit in unpublished loan agreements. IMF programme documents give system-wide prudential benchmarks, not counterparty covenants.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-promising covenant-level intelligence from this cell; the realistic ceiling is transaction structure plus system-level prudential conditionality.

coverage_gaps.description: Per-institution statutory financial statements (individual licensed banks' IFRS reports) were not located as a browsable NBU index; only aggregated/grouped data was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the Ukrainian Unified Financial Reporting System (Єдина система фінансової звітності / СФЗ, NSSMC-and-Ministry-of-Finance operated) as the likely host of per-entity taxonomy-tagged bank statements, and check individual bank IR pages as the fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: All NBU endpoints in this slice are unverified for automated liveness because the host returned 403 to the tooling used.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic verification pass with a realistic User-Agent and, if needed, a headless browser; classify 403s as bot-defended-live rather than dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Payments-market statistical series from the NBU (card transaction volumes, POS/ATM terminal counts, cashless payment share) were not pinned to specific dataset URLs in this slice; only the payments registers and oversight pages were captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted follow-up on uk terms: 'Показники розвитку безготівкових розрахунків', 'Платіжні картки та платіжна інфраструктура', 'Оверсайт платіжних систем звіт', plus the corresponding NBUStatService endpoints.

coverage_gaps.description: English mirrors were confirmed to exist for the main NBU sections (/en/statistic, /en/stability/report, /en/news/all) but were not systematically enumerated per source.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Record both /ua/ and /en/ variants for every NBU source; the en edition of the Financial Stability Report and Banking Sector Review often lags the uk edition by days.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival strategy identified for NBU PDFs whose URLs carry mutable ?v= cache-busting suffixes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror NBU PDFs locally on publication and record the canonical filename pattern (e.g. Banking_Sector_Review_YYYY-MM.pdf, FSR_YYYY-Hn_eng.pdf) rather than the versioned URL; consider Wayback Machine as a secondary archive.

coverage_gaps.description: Sense Bank disclosure tree unmapped (no reporting page, no confirmed IFRS PDF).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a headless site-map crawl of sensebank.ua (paths to try: /about, /pro-bank, /zvitnist, /rozkryttya-informatsiyi) and pull its SMIDA issuer record by EDRPOU 23494714 as a fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: Bond-listing-venue disclosure (offering circulars, noteholder notices) for Oschadbank eurobonds/LPNs not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Euronext Dublin / LSE listing-venue archives and Irish Stock Exchange filings for XS1273034444 and related ISINs; also check the trustee's notice page.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI counterparty disclosure (EBRD, IFC, World Bank project pages carrying state-bank due-diligence and covenant material) not yet catalogued in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass over ebrd.com project summaries and disclosures.ifc.org for Oschadbank / Ukrgasbank / Sense Bank projects — these are pointer-and-direct hybrids with investor-grade detail.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage is thin for Ukrgasbank and Sense Bank — searches surfaced only uk-language reporting pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check for /en/ mirrors on ukrgasbank.com and sensebank.ua and record whether an English disclosure track exists at all; if absent, log it as a structural finding for privatisation-marketing readiness.

coverage_gaps.description: NBU (bank.gov.ua) per-bank supervisory statistics and NSSMC (stockmarket.gov.ua) disclosure portal were not directly probed in this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe bank.gov.ua statistical dataset pages and the NSSMC disclosure portal as pointer sources that normalise all four issuers into one machine-readable feed.

coverage_gaps.description: The actual member-list pages of НАБУ, АУБ and УАФІК were identified but never rendered — only their URLs/navigation were captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-crawl https://nabu.ua/ (via sitemap), https://aub.org.ua/pro-asotsiatsiiu/aub-members/ and fintechua.org members route with a rate-limited headless browser and extract full member tables with outbound URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: No association was found covering POS/terminal vendors, processors, ATM operators or cash-in-transit — the payment-infrastructure supply side.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search uk terms 'асоціація процесингових компаній', 'асоціація операторів банкоматів', 'постачальники платіжного обладнання Україна асоціація'; also check IT Ukraine Association membership, which was observed to admit payment services (UAPAY).

coverage_gaps.description: English mirrors exist (aub.org.ua/en, fintechua.org/en, vaks.org.ua/en) but were not compared against the Ukrainian versions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Diff uk vs en member pages — English mirrors are often stale, so the uk page should be treated as canonical; record the lag as a data-quality flag.

coverage_gaps.description: All rosters found are point-in-time; no archive of past membership was located, so entries/exits cannot be reconstructed retrospectively.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Seed a baseline snapshot now and query the Wayback Machine for historical captures of the ЄМА, АУБ and НАБУ member pages to build a back-series.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unclear whether ЄМА and УАФІК flagship reports are fully public or members-only/form-gated; only a mirrored 2023 fintech catalogue PDF was located as an open copy.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Attempt direct download of the latest editions from the association sites; if gated, log as a partial-access source and rely on trade-media summaries plus the mirrored PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: No regional or niche Ukrainian financial outlets (e.g. Ekonomichna Pravda's regional peers, Telegram/YouTube analyst channels run by banking journalists) were scouted; these often break results stories ahead of the mainstream desks.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-on pass targeting Ukrainian banking-journalist Telegram channels and newsletter products, and check each mainstream outlet's own Telegram mirror.

coverage_gaps.description: No archive or backfill route was established for any outlet — pagination limits, sitemap availability and whether historic league tables remain online are unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe sitemap.xml and tag-page pagination for minfin.com.ua, epravda.com.ua, mind.ua and forbes.ua; register key ranking URLs with a web archive for longitudinal comparison.

coverage_gaps.description: Interfax-Ukraine and Opendatabot both gate their most structured outputs behind commercial subscriptions/APIs; terms and pricing were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Request commercial terms from Interfax-Ukraine and Opendatabot before designing any high-frequency collection against them.

coverage_gaps.description: Media rankings in this cell almost all derive from the same upstream NBU statutory reporting, but the exact NBU dataset and its release calendar were not mapped in this cell (it belongs to a regulator cell).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-link this slice to the regulator/NBU cell so media items can be anchored to the primary release date and used mainly for interpretation and materiality signal, not as a data source of record.
coverage_gaps.coverage_dimension: source class balance (indirect-heavy, thin on direct)

coverage_gaps.description: No candidate in this slice was fetched directly; all were identified via search-result evidence, so liveness, paywall depth and robots/ToS specifics remain unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic verification pass over every URL, and specifically capture robots.txt and ToS for youcontrol.com.ua, opendatabot.ua, clarity-project.info and vkursi.pro.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice establishes the register/aggregator channels but does not yet produce the actual list of EDRPOU codes for Ukrainian banks and licensed payment institutions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-join NBU's registers of banks and payment infrastructure participants with the ЄДР open dataset and GLEIF UA records to build a canonical entity table keyed on EDRPOU + LEI.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale assumes aggregators preserve documents after issuer sites go offline, but no evidence was gathered on whether any of them retain original PDF filings versus only normalised data fields.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test one bank's historical annual report retrieval on Clarity Project, Opendatabot and SMIDA to determine which retains original documents versus derived indicators.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Ukrainian registers is thin: aggregator English interfaces exist (YouControl /en/) but were not assessed for field parity with the Ukrainian version.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compare a bank dossier in uk and en on YouControl to check whether financial and ownership fields are dropped in translation.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller or niche Ukrainian register aggregators (e.g. ring.org.ua, edrpou.info-type sites) were probed but only edrpou.ubki.ua surfaced with evidence; the long tail of mirror sites is unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run additional Ukrainian-language queries for 'перевірка контрагента онлайн безкоштовно' and 'реєстр компаній України' to enumerate second-tier mirrors that may host cached filings.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice catalogued the archive INFRASTRUCTURE and the regulator-side continuity registers, but did not enumerate individual bank/PSP IR domains and their historical URL patterns (only PUMB was reached concretely).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a domain inventory from the NBU/DGF registers (all banks 2013-present, incl. liquidated), record each historical IR/disclosure URL, then run Wayback CDX per domain with a pre-2022-02-24 cut-off to establish the baseline.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank payment sector (PSPs, acquirers, payment-terminal operators, money-transfer systems) has no archival source identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile the NBU register of payment-service providers, then proactively submit each PSP's site to web.archive.org save-page-now on a schedule; retroactive recovery is impossible once a private site is deleted.

coverage_gaps.description: Occupied-territory / Crimea-Donbas successor institutions and their disclosure are entirely uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scope a separate, legally-reviewed cell for this: sanctions screening first, then decide whether collection is permissible at all; if it is, favour third-party and archived material over direct contact with the entities.

coverage_gaps.description: The 2014-2016 bank-failure wave (which killed roughly half the banking system's institutions) is only indirectly covered via the NBU history page and Minfin aggregator; no verified archived source of those banks' own annual reports was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each bank on the NBU post-2014 exit list, run a CDX sweep for PDFs on its former domain and cross-check DGF liquidation pages; record 'never captured' explicitly as a permanent loss.

coverage_gaps.description: No forward-looking preservation routine is specified — the run treats archives as read-only, but the highest-value action for a wartime market is CREATING captures before loss.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a recurring save-page-now job over the bank/PSP disclosure URL inventory, plus a local PDF mirror with checksums, so the project itself becomes a source of record.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language sources dominate the archiving-infrastructure half of this cell; Ukrainian-language querying produced almost nothing on web archiving as such.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: In future runs, pair Ukrainian register vocabulary (розкриття інформації, річна інформація емітента, банки що ліквідуються, припинення діяльності) with English archiving vocabulary (wayback, CDX, WARC, mirror) rather than translating one into the other.

coverage_gaps.description: International core-banking and card-processing platform vendors (BPC/SmartVista, OpenWay/Way4, Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Diasoft, Colvir, ITTI Digital) have no confirmed Ukrainian-bank engagement mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run per-vendor queries in both languages, including Cyrillic transliterations ('Смарт Віста', 'Вей4', 'Теменос', 'Колвір', 'Флексk'юб'), plus site-restricted searches over each vendor's own customer/case-study pages for 'Ukraine'.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM hardware OEM and ATM-managed-services presence in Ukraine is mapped only through one local service company (Printec Ukraine); no OEM-side Ukrainian customer evidence collected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify the Ukrainian legal entities of the ATM OEMs and their local partners via the state register / YouControl by KVED and by name fragments; then pull their Prozorro award history as supplier (Prozorro exposes supplier-side award records, not just buyer-side).

coverage_gaps.description: Cards/personalisation, cash-handling OEM and ATM-OEM segments were probed largely in English; Ukrainian-language equivalents were not exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and run a Ukrainian glossary pass: 'персоналізація платіжних карток', 'виробництво банківських карток', 'рециркулятори готівки', 'системи обробки готівки', 'сервісне обслуговування банкоматів', 'постачання банкоматів'.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor LinkedIn company feeds and conference/exhibition materials (e.g. Ukrainian banking-IT forums, NBU-adjacent industry events, PSM Awards nominee dossiers) were not systematically harvested, though these often carry customer names never posted to the corporate site.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add LinkedIn company pages for the vendor watchlist (CS, UNITY-BARS, ProFIX, UPC, UKRCARD, Printec Ukraine) and harvest annual conference agendas/speaker affiliations as an actor-map refresh.

coverage_gaps.description: Prozorro was identified but only used through the web UI; the supplier-side view and the open API/bulk exports were not exercised, and buyer EDRPOU codes for the state banks were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate EDRPOU codes for PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank and Sense Bank; pull all tenders and awards by those buyers and by relevant DK021 CPV codes (30123200-9 ATMs, and the POS/terminal and banking-software codes) through the API for a structured, dated supplier ledger.

coverage_gaps.description: Most recovered vendor-bank evidence clusters in 2018-2024; recent (2025-2026) vendor announcements about Ukrainian bank engagements were only lightly sampled, chiefly around open banking.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run the vendor watchlist with explicit 2025/2026 date anchors and monitor the NBU open-banking go-live (from 1 Aug 2025) as a forcing event that should generate a wave of vendor-side integration announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: Only DK 021:2015 66110000-4 was empirically confirmed in searches. Adjacent codes covering payment-terminal supply (POS hardware), processing services, cash-in-transit and card personalisation were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the full DK021/CPV code list for the payments value chain (66110000, 66172000 financial transaction processing, 66600000 treasury, 30140000/30160000 calculating & card machines, 79710000 security/CIT) and run code-scoped ProZorro API sweeps.

coverage_gaps.description: No systematic enumeration of the key buyer entities (Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, Sense/Ukreximbank as buyers of IT, Ministry of Finance, Treasury, Pension Fund, oblast administrations, municipal transport operators procuring fare acquiring).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile an EDRPOU list of state banks, ministries, PFU and top-20 municipalities; run buyer-scoped ProZorro and spending.gov.ua queries.

coverage_gaps.description: Wartime direct-contracting exemptions ('особливості' regime under martial law) allow many contracts to be reported without an open tender; this pass did not map how such banking contracts are disclosed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Study the martial-law procurement 'Особливості' rules and identify the report-of-contract (звіт про договір) object type in the API, which is where most banking awards may now sit.

coverage_gaps.description: Russian-language variants of key terms (эквайринг, расчетно-кассовое обслуживание) were not searched, and some legacy records or aggregator pages may use them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ru-language variants to the query set for historical coverage, while treating uk as primary.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal-level procurement portals and transport-ticketing operators (e-ticket acquiring) were not explored, despite being a major non-state channel for payment-services awards.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from ProZorro buyer names in the e-ticket/transport segment to municipal sites and operator pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian- and German-language filings of the parent groups (OTP's BSE/Hungarian filings, RBI's German-language Geschäftsbericht, ProCredit's German annual financial statements) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a hu/de search leg using terms such as 'ukrajnai leánybank', 'szegmens', 'Segmentberichterstattung Ukraine', and check the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE/BÉT) and German Bundesanzeiger filing channels.

coverage_gaps.description: Other foreign-parent banks in Ukraine were not enumerated systematically (e.g. Citibank Ukraine, ING Ukraine, Deutsche Bank representative presence, Sense Bank post-nationalisation history, TAScombank-type mixed ownership).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use the NBU institutions register plus its foreign-capital classification to build the full parent-group watchlist, then check each parent's IR site for a Ukraine country annex.

coverage_gaps.description: Regulated-filing venues for the parents (Vienna Stock Exchange / OeKB ad-hoc disclosure, Budapest Stock Exchange filings, EU ESAP/OAM national storage mechanisms) were not scouted; only issuer-hosted IR pages were.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the official appointed mechanisms (OeKB Emittenten, BSE bet.hu company filings, Bundesanzeiger) as machine-readable, timestamped alternatives to issuer PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: Structured data artefacts (RBI XLSM results file, OTP iXBRL annual report packs, ESEF/iXBRL filings) were identified only by reference, not located at a stable URL.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and pin the direct XLSM/iXBRL download URLs per issuer; these give clean per-country time series and remove PDF-parsing risk.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs recorded here come from search results or a single fetch; liveness, paywalling and robots/ToS posture were not verified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass; treat any 403/timeout (notably investing.com, cbonds, quartr) as bot-defended rather than dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Tascombank's own «розкриття інформації»/annual-report page (licence holder for izibank, absorbed Sportbank) was not pinned down; only an ESG subdomain surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted queries «ТАСКОМБАНК річна фінансова звітність», «Таскомбанк розкриття інформації» and crawl tascombank.ua site navigation directly.

coverage_gaps.description: Several other domestic privately owned banks in scope were not reached in this pass: ОКСІ БАНК, Банк «Глобус», Агропросперіс Банк, Банк Восток's peers such as Індустріалбанк, Банк «Український капітал», Полтава-банк, Банк «Портал», Кредитвест, ПІН Банк, Банк Січ successors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the NBU register of operating banks, filter to private domestic ownership via the structure-of-ownership register, then locate each bank's disclosure heading individually.

coverage_gaps.description: No web-archive strategy was established for banks whose disclosure pages disappear on liquidation (Concord, Sportbank, Sich, Ukrbudinvestbank).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Wayback Machine / archive.today lookup step keyed to each defunct bank's historical domain, plus the Deposit Guarantee Fund (fg.gov.ua) liquidation dossiers.

coverage_gaps.description: Only Universal Bank's newsroom was identified; the press/newsroom sections of PUMB, A-Bank, Credit Dnipro, Vostok and Alliance were not individually pinned, and neobank founders' Telegram channels (a genuine primary disclosure channel for monobank) were not mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate each bank's /news or /press section and evaluate RSS availability; separately assess monobank's official Telegram/social channels as an indirect but high-tempo source.

coverage_gaps.description: English mirrors were only confirmed for PUMB, MTB Bank, Bank Alliance and Radabank; most private banks appear to disclose in Ukrainian only, and some legacy PDFs are served under /ru/ paths.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Default the collection pipeline to Ukrainian with OCR/translation downstream; do not assume an EN mirror exists or is complete.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed machine-readable successor to the v1 open-data API for regulated information published after 30/06/2021.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe smida.gov.ua for an API or structured export behind /db/feed (RSS/JSON/XML), and inspect the file paths /files/feed/[date]/[uuid]/ for a deterministic naming convention that permits bulk retrieval.

coverage_gaps.description: No sector filter in the issuer index means the bank/payments issuer population is not yet enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an EDRPOU watchlist from the NBU register of licensed banks and payment-service providers, then resolve each against smida.gov.ua/db/emitent and /db/prof to produce the definitive issuer subset.

coverage_gaps.description: Bond prospectus retrieval path for bank issuers is hypothesised, not confirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open the stockmarket.gov.ua 'Проспекти' navigation node and the /db/feed report-type dropdown, identify the exact prospectus report-type code, and test a filtered query for a known bank bond issuer.

coverage_gaps.description: The disclosure database and all filings are Ukrainian-only; NSSMC's English site covers policy and press but not filing content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for Ukrainian-language parsing and a controlled uk→en term map for filing types (річна інформація, проміжна інформація, особлива інформація, проспект, звіт про управління).

coverage_gaps.description: Regulated information may be published via multiple authorised publishers, and only SMIDA has been identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the NSSMC register of authorised regulated-information publishers (via the Положення z1307-23 references and the NSSMC licensing section) and add each publisher's feed to the monitoring set.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank payments companies are largely outside the issuer disclosure perimeter.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not rely on this cell for payments-actor discovery; flag to the coordinating cells that NBU registers and the ЄДР are the correct venue, and use this cell only where a payments firm has issued bonds.

coverage_gaps.description: Securities-regulator disclosure channel (NSSMC / SMIDA / stockmarket.gov.ua) not yet mapped for payment-sector bond issuers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated pass to locate the issuer-disclosure search interface and pull filings for NovaPay Credit and any other PSP-affiliated issuer; add the NSSMC site itself as a pointer source.

coverage_gaps.description: Brand-to-legal-entity resolution is incomplete: only Portmone (EDRPOU 31868613) and Fondy (ТОВ ФК 'ЕЛАЄНС') were resolved. EasyPay, City24 (ФК 'Свіфт Гарант'), IBOX terminals, LeoGaming Pay and iPay.ua lack confirmed EDRPOU codes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the full EDRPOU watchlist from the NBU payment infrastructure register export, then join to data.gov.ua financial-statement datasets and Opendatabot alerts.

coverage_gaps.description: No audit-firm or credit-rating primary source captured. Standard-Rating (Стандарт-Рейтинг) assigned uaAA to NovaPay bonds but its own publication site was not visited.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Ukrainian rating agencies (Standard-Rating, IBI-Rating, Credit-Rating) as direct sources; their rating reports carry financial detail on non-disclosing PSPs.

coverage_gaps.description: Almost all substantive disclosure in this cell is Ukrainian-only; English coverage is limited to NBU translations and a NovaPay English profile.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Ukrainian as the primary collection language for this cell; do not rely on English mirrors, which lag and omit register and enforcement detail.

coverage_gaps.description: Court and insolvency registries (Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень) not covered, despite litigation and licence-revocation being the main public events in this sector.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add reyestr.court.gov.ua as an indirect source and monitor for the PSP EDRPOU watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: Corporate homepages for UPC (upc.ua) and TAS Link (taslink.ua) were inferred from company names and asset paths rather than opened during this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over these domains and correct the canonical URL before scheduling collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Independent ATM deployers and cash-in/self-service terminal networks beyond UkrCard (e.g. bank-independent ATM operators, IBOX/self-service networks) and the merchant-acquiring PSP layer (Portmone, Fondy, LiqPay, Platon, NovaPay) were not systematically enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated sweep of the NBU register's payment-service-provider and infrastructure-operator sections plus uk-language searches for 'мережа банкоматів', 'платіжні термінали самообслуговування', 'інтернет-еквайринг провайдер'.

coverage_gaps.description: No open-data/API endpoint for NBU card and POS statistics was identified in this pass; only PDFs and HTML pages were found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe bank.gov.ua's statistics API / open-data section (and data.gov.ua) for a structured payments dataset.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language NBU payments pages were not sampled; the en mirror may be less bot-defended and easier to collect for headline series.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test bank.gov.ua/en/payments equivalents and compare content parity with the uk pages.

coverage_gaps.description: The full list of per-bank *.fg.gov.ua liquidation subdomain slugs was not enumerated; only five instances (ukrinbank, bnk, concord, ibox, plus the /banki-shcho-likviduyutsya path-based entries) were observed, and the register page is paginated with a JS 'load more' control.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated crawl of https://www.fg.gov.ua/banki-v-upravlinni-fondu/banki-shcho-likviduyutsya and the three sibling registers, with pagination handled, to produce the authoritative slug/subdomain list. Note that both path-based (/banki-shcho-likviduyutsya/<slug>) and subdomain-based (<slug>.fg.gov.ua) addressing appear to exist and should be reconciled.

coverage_gaps.description: Prozorro.Sale's open-data/API endpoints for the ЦБД1 bankrupt-bank asset stream could not be documented because both relevant pages returned 403 on fetch.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retry via a browser-based fetch or with realistic headers; consult the Prozorro.Sale developer documentation and the ФГВФО organiser profile at https://prozorro.sale/organizers/fgvfo/ to confirm whether lot-level data is exposed as a public API.

coverage_gaps.description: Court-registry coverage of liquidation and resolution disputes was not searched. Shareholders of several resolved banks litigate their market withdrawal for years (the DGF publishes rebuttals on this), and the Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень would carry those rulings.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a scouting pass on reyestr.court.gov.ua (and the DGF's own litigation section) for case law naming the Fund as liquidator, keyed on 'виведення з ринку', 'ліквідація банку', 'ФГВФО'.

coverage_gaps.description: Alternative electronic auction platforms besides Prozorro.Sale — notably СЕТАМ and the individual accredited electronic trading platforms named in DGF auction passports (e.g. TOV 'NVP Informatsiyni Tekhnolohii') — were identified only in passing and not scouted as sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the accredited-platform list referenced in DGF auction passports and assess whether any publishes results not mirrored on Prozorro.Sale.

coverage_gaps.description: DGF social/messaging channels (Telegram, Facebook, YouTube) under /novini-ta-media were not enumerated. In Ukraine these are often the fastest publication channel for resolution announcements.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch https://www.fg.gov.ua/novini-ta-media to capture official social handles and assess them as low-latency event feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: The English-language DGF site was mapped, but it was not established how far behind the Ukrainian site it runs, nor whether annual reports are published in English at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compare the /en statistics and reports pages against their Ukrainian counterparts on as-of dates; if no English annual report exists, record it as an EN negative finding and plan for machine translation of the Ukrainian PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: Depth of the DGF press-release archive was observed to at least page 30 but the earliest available date and whether the pre-2015 site (old fg.gov.ua URL scheme, e.g. /dlia-vkladnykiv/91-news-uk/...) is still reachable were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe the oldest pagination pages and a sample legacy-scheme URL to determine the true archive floor and whether a web-archive backfill is required for the 2014-2016 failure wave.

coverage_gaps.description: The full Section IV list of audit entities entitled to audit public-interest entities (and therefore banks) has not been enumerated; only Big Four plus Grant Thornton, Baker Tilly, BDO and one local firm were identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the data.gov.ua register dataset, filter to Section IV, and use it as the master seed list for per-firm transparency-report discovery.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified auditor→bank matrix was built for the ~60 licensed Ukrainian banks; only isolated examples (Universal Bank, Bank Globus/Baker Tilly, TASCOMBANK/MTB/Kredobank tender notices) were observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-join three independent sources — bank-hosted IFRS opinions, SMIDA auditinfo forms, and ProZorro awards for state banks — and reconcile discrepancies against APOB register status.

coverage_gaps.description: Wartime effects on audit timing (deadline extensions, martial-law reporting relief, delayed or unavailable opinions for banks in occupied/resolved status) were not investigated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search NBU and APOB notices for 'воєнний стан' + 'аудит' / 'подовження строку' to map deadline shifts 2022–2026 before treating a missing opinion as non-disclosure.

coverage_gaps.description: Payments-sector coverage (payment institutions, e-money issuers, PSPs under the Law on Payment Services) was not separately probed for audit obligations and auditors — this cell's searches were bank-centric.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run uk queries on 'аудит платіжної установи', 'надавач платіжних послуг аудиторський звіт НБУ' to test whether an analogous auditor pointer layer exists for non-bank payment firms.

coverage_gaps.description: The audit committee / ревізійна комісія and corporate-governance disclosures inside bank annual reports (auditor tenure, non-audit fees, rotation dates) were not scouted, though they are the counterpart disclosure to the auditor's own transparency report.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass over bank 'Звіт про управління' and 'Корпоративне управління' pages for auditor tenure and fee disclosures.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral European DFIs that co-invest alongside the majors in Ukrainian financial services were identified as co-investors (Proparco, Swedfund, Finnfund, IFU, and by extension KfW/DEG, FMO, BGK) but their own disclosure registers were not scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass over Proparco, FMO, DEG/KfW, Swedfund, Finnfund, IFU and BGK project databases filtered on Ukraine + financial sector.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI independent accountability and evaluation arms (IFC CAO, EBRD IPAM and EvD, World Bank Inspection Panel, IEG) were not systematically scouted. These publish the most candid assessments of financial-intermediary lending.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout CAO, IPAM, Inspection Panel and IEG case registers for Ukraine financial-intermediary cases and evaluations.

coverage_gaps.description: API/bulk-download endpoints were not confirmed for IFC disclosures, EBRD projects, MIGA or EIB. Only the World Bank is known to expose documented public APIs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Technical probe for JSON endpoints, IATI publications and open-data exports per institution; record robots.txt and rate limits before scheduling collection.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI annual reports and Ukraine country strategies (EBRD Country Strategy for Ukraine, IFC country strategy, World Bank CPF) were not individually scouted, and their Ukrainian-language summaries — which the cell rationale assumes exist — were not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the EBRD Ukraine Country Strategy, WB Country Partnership Framework and their uk-language summaries; confirm whether Ukrainian versions are published at all.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI shareholding/equity stakes in Ukrainian banks specifically (as opposed to lending and guarantees) were only partially evidenced — the clearest case found was IFC's Ukrgasbank loan with an option to convert into up to 20 percent equity.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted search per state bank (Ukrgasbank, Oschadbank, PrivatBank, Sense Bank) for IFI equity or convertible instruments, and cross-check against NBU ownership-structure disclosures.

briefs: The National Bank of Ukraine is a single, unusually dense A1 node: it operates the State Register of Banks directory, the supervisory-statistics section, a documented OpenData REST API (NBUStatService, plus NBU_BankInfo for the bank directory), the semi-annual Financial Stability Report, the quarterly Banking Sector Review with a fully predictable PDF filename pattern, and an active press service that publishes sector profit aggregates ahead of the media cycle. Because the NBU is also Ukraine's payments regulator, the same domain carries the payment-infrastructure register, licensing of payment service providers and technological operators, and FMI oversight categorisations — covering both halves of the sector scope. The practical constraint is access, not availability: every plain fetch of bank.gov.ua returned HTTP 403 in this run, so collection should use browser-like headers or a headless browser and lean on the data.gov.ua CKAN mirrors of NBU datasets, which are unobstructed. The main substantive gap is per-institution statutory financial statements, which appear to be migrating into Ukraine's unified Financial Reporting System (Єдина СФЗ) taxonomy rather than living as a browsable NBU index.

Ukraine's four state-owned banks publish IR-grade material, but through statutory disclosure pages rather than any true investor-relations function: PrivatBank via its financial-statements page plus a genuinely IR-quality English Integrated Report series, Oschadbank via 'звітність емітента цінних паперів' and an English news feed, and Ukrgasbank via the most complete and best-structured IFRS tree of the four (annual audited, interim, and regular issuer information). The Ministry of Finance acts as a shareholder-side aggregator hosting copies of all four banks' reports plus monthly performance decks, and SMIDA is the machine-readable statutory backstop keyed by EDRPOU. Weak points are Sense Bank, whose disclosure tree could not be mapped from search alone, and eurobond/LPN-specific investor documentation, which does not appear to live on issuer sites. Access is complicated by bot defences (mof.gov.ua 403, oschadbank.ua redirect loop) and by heavy English-language name collision with unrelated 'Privatbank' entities in Luxembourg, Latvia and Austria.

Ukraine has no compulsory SRO layer in banking or payments, so the actor population must be assembled by unioning several voluntary association rosters: three banking associations (НАБУ, АУБ, УКБС), the payments association ЄМА, the fintech association УАФІК, and non-bank bodies ВАФК/ВАКС/АФІ. The single richest page found is ЄМА's member directory, which enumerates card schemes, ~40 banks, PSPs, marketplaces and a credit bureau as linked entries and snowballs straight into corporate press/IR pages; АУБ adds a members list plus its own banking-statistics and Power BI analytics layer, and УАФІК's annual 'Каталог фінтех-компаній України' doubles as both a company roster and market-sizing study. Access is the main constraint rather than availability: nabu.ua rate-limited (429), fintechua.org is client-side rendered, and ukbs.org.ua failed DNS once — all treated as unverified, not dead, and all needing a rate-limited headless-browser pass. Registry cards (EDRPOU captured for all seven associations) and the NBU payment-systems participant register give an independent cross-check on any roster that turns out to be gated or stale.

Ukrainian business and financial media form a dense, fast, and largely open aggregation layer over bank disclosure: Minfin, Forbes Ukraine and Mind.ua each run methodology-backed recurring bank league tables, while Ekonomichna Pravda, Interfax-Ukraine, RBC-Ukraine, NV Business and FinClub push quarterly profit rankings within days of NBU data release. Interfax-Ukraine is the standout dual-purpose source — an English-language earnings wire plus a press-release channel that banks and PSPs use as a de-facto investor-relations distribution point. The main structural weakness is the payments side: no Ukrainian outlet appears to run a recurring PSP or acquiring league table, leaving psm7.com (PaySpace Magazine) as the only dedicated trade title and pushing payments financials back onto regulator and company sources. Almost everything here is indirect and traces to the same upstream NBU reporting, so the cell is best used for materiality signal, entity discovery and translation rather than as data of record; Opendatabot is the most useful pointer for jumping from a media table back to structured underlying figures.

Ukraine's register-and-aggregator layer is unusually rich: a statutory core (ЄДР via usr.minjust.gov.ua free search plus a bulk open dataset on data.gov.ua whose access was restricted in 2022 and reported restored in January 2026) sits under four mature commercial aggregators — YouControl, Opendatabot, Clarity Project and Vkursi — each of which normalises registration data, ownership and financial-statement indicators keyed on EDRPOU and each of which can enumerate every bank and payment company by KVED 64.x/66.x. For actual filings rather than indicators, SMIDA/stockmarket.gov.ua is the statutory disclosure archive holding issuer annual reports (banks file on a bank-specific form, deadline 30 April), and GLEIF's LEI Search plus Golden Copy/Level 2 files provide the international identity and group-ownership backbone for UA financial entities. The binding constraints are commercial: financial statements and APIs on all four aggregators are paywalled, so the wartime archive value of this cell depends on licence terms, not on technical access. Highest-leverage next step is joining the ЄДР bulk dataset with NBU registers and GLEIF UA records into one canonical EDRPOU+LEI entity table, then testing which aggregators retain original documents rather than only derived fields.

Ukraine has no national web archive, so archival continuity for banking and payments disclosure rests on foreign infrastructure — principally the Internet Archive (whose CDX API is the workhorse for recovering pre-2022 IR pages and PDF annual reports by domain), with SUCHO, Archive-It and archive.today as partial supplements of uneven coverage and accessibility. The strongest Ukrainian-side continuity assets are not archives at all but statutory repositories that outlive the institution: SMIDA/NSSMC holds each bank's full issuer-disclosure history independently of its website, the Deposit Guarantee Fund custodies the record of liquidated banks and publishes explicitly dated archives of the member-bank population, and the NBU's since-2014 reorganisation/liquidation register plus the Ministry of Finance's state-bank reporting provide the actor map and a government-hosted mirror. Ukrainian-language search was productive for this register layer and near-barren for archiving concepts, where English terminology carries the recall. The main unmet risks are the non-bank payment sector, which has no statutory repository and can only be preserved by proactive capture before deletion, and the occupied-territory successor institutions, which no source in this slice reaches.

Ukraine's vendor-side disclosure landscape splits cleanly into three tiers. First, domestic banking-software and processing vendors publish the richest indirect intelligence: CS Ltd (CBS B2, self-described #1 core banking system in Ukraine, naming OTP Bank, Bank Lviv and BISbank), UNITY-BARS (ABS BARS, COPR2/Corplight), UPC and UKRCARD on the processing side, and ProFIX on payments connectivity — their press centres and case-study pages are effectively the public register of which private bank runs what. Second, international vendors disclose Ukraine only sporadically but with high reliability when they do: Tietoevry's regulated releases document the UPC open-banking partnership and the earlier Card Suite cross-border acquiring launch, while no Ukrainian engagement could be found for the ATM OEMs, BPC/OpenWay/Temenos, or the card-personalisation majors — an unresolved gap rather than a confirmed absence. Third, because PrivatBank, Oschadbank and Ukrgasbank are state-owned, Prozorro carries genuine hardware procurement records (ATM and ATM-component lots, mobile POS/acquiring service contracts) that name suppliers and prices, giving a hard-evidence baseline against which private-bank capex can be inferred; local trade press (PaySpace Magazine, FinClub, AIN.UA) and the state company register via YouControl complete the actor map. Priority next steps are the Prozorro API by buyer EDRPOU and CPV code, and a Ukrainian-language glossary pass over the ATM, cards and cash-handling segments, which remain English-only and therefore under-covered.

Ukraine's public-procurement channel is unusually rich for banking and payments intelligence: ProZorro (prozorro.gov.ua plus the OpenProcurement API and BI Prozorro) publishes tender notices and award records under DK 021:2015 66110000-4, and confirmed live examples cover internet acquiring, settlement-cash servicing, payroll banking and QR/mobile payment acceptance — each naming the incumbent bank, the contract value and the expiry date. Spending.gov.ua (E-Data) adds the ex-post layer of actual treasury payments and signed contracts, while Prozorro.Sale and the DGF cabinet cover the distressed-bank asset side. Around the core sit pointers and control layers worth tracking: Clarity Project and DoZorro for entity resolution and snowballing, AMCU appeal decisions and State Audit Service monitoring for contested awards, and TED, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, EBRD ECEPP and World Bank STEP plans for EU/IFI-funded work that never enters ProZorro. The main structural risks are the martial-law direct-contracting regime, which may move most banking awards into report-of-contract objects rather than open tenders, and the apparent absence of a standalone tender for payment acceptance inside the Diia ecosystem.

Ukraine-specific bank earnings in this cell flow through two structurally different channels that must both be collected. The group channel — RBI (Vienna), OTP (Budapest) and ProCredit Holding (Frankfurt) — carries Ukraine as a named country segment or subsidiary chapter inside English-language annual/quarterly reports, results files and earnings calls; OTP's quarterly 'Summary of results' PDF series is the single most granular and most automatable artefact found.
